documents.title: Palladium-catalyzed C–P cross-coupling of allenic alcohols with H-phosphonates leading to 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes

Palladium-catalyzed C–P cross-coupling of allenic
alcohols with H-phosphonates leading to
2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes†
Shanshan Hu, a Wenyu Sun, a Junhong Chen, b Sipei Li, a Runmin Zhao, b
Pengxiang Xu,* a Yuxing Gao
 *a and Yufen Zhao
 a
The first facile, eﬃcient, atom-economical and regioselective palladium-
catalyzed direct C–P cross-coupling of unprotected allenic alcohols
with H-phosphonates for the one-pot synthesis of structurally diverse
multisubstituted 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes was developed. This
strategy would enrich the allene chemistry and afford new scaffolds to
construct complex molecular skeletons.
The construction of various kinds of organophosphorus compounds
is a fundamental and significant topic in modern synthetic
chemistry due to their broad applicability in biochemistry, pharma-
ceuticals, materials science and organic synthesis.
1 Phosphinoyl 1,3-
butadienes as representative functionalized phosphorus compounds
are an important class of butadiene-containing valuable precursors
in synthetic chemistry, which could be readily transformed to other
useful compounds such as all ylic phosphonates obtained via
Michael addition with nucleophiles,
2 alkenylphosphonates aﬀorded
through cycloaddition,3 and vinyl allenes yielded through addition
reaction with aldehydes.4 Moreover, they are also potentially useful
intermediates for P-ligand preparation.5 Not surprisingly, consider-
able endeavor has been focused on the synthesis of 2-phosphinoyl-
1,3-butadienes; however, the method for the preparation of these
unique motifs, especially multisu bstituted 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-
butadienes, is quite rare to date and generally more challenging.
In 1996, the procedure for the preparation of (1,3-dien-2-yl) diphenyl-
phosphine oxides from allenic alcohols and air- and moisture-
sensitive chlorodiphenylphosphine as raw materials was developed
via [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangements (Scheme 1a).
6 However, it
heavily suﬀered from the use of unstable and toxic phosphorus
chlorides, a large amount of bases, poor functional group compat-
ibility and low yields, thus limiting its application. In 2005, Han’s
group disclosed the first nickel-catalyzed addition of P(O)H com-
pounds to propargyl alcohols for the synthesis of 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-
butadienes (Scheme 1b), but its general use poses severe limitations
due to limited substrate scope and poor regioselectivity giving mixed
products of Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov adducts.
7 Recently,
Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of allenylphosphine oxides
with arylboronic acids and the photoredox catalysis of allenylphos-
phine oxides with diaryl disulfides leading to (1,3-dien-2-yl)
diphenylphosphine oxides were revealed (Scheme 1c).
8 However,
these methods required the pre-preparation of complex and
inaccessible allenylphosphine oxides as substrates and did not
afford 1-substituted 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes. Therefore,
new and economic methodologies for efficient access to highly

substituted 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes with broad substrate
compatibility and excellent regioselectivity are still desired.
Allenic alcohols, animportant class of allene compounds with
a distinctive substructure of a hydroxyl group and two cumulative
carbon–carbon double bonds, are readily available
9 and versatile
building blocks for making valuable molecular skeletons, such as
dihydrofurans,
10 vinylic oxiranes,11 unsaturated ketones,12 and
1,3-butadienes.13 In addition, from economic and environmental
points of view, the direct use of u nprotected allenic alcohols as
starting materials is highly attractive for modern organic synthesis
as water is the only byproduct in some transformations13b,14 and
due to their prominent advantages of step and atom economy.
N e v e r t h e l e s s ,t ot h eb e s to fo u rk n o w l e d g e ,n oe x a m p l eo f
2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadiene synthesis via transition-metal-
catalyzed direct coupling of allenic alcohols with P(O)H com-
pounds was reported. As part of our ongoing endeavor to develop
environmentally benign novel approaches for P–C bond forma-
tion,
15 herein, we demonstrate the first example of Pd-catalyzed
direct cross-coupling of various allenic alcohols with H-phos-
phonates to access structurally diverse 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-
butadienes, providing a quite convenient and efficient tool to
construct a wide range of multisubstituted 2-phosphinoyl buta-
diene frameworks along with the production of new P–C, C–C and
CQC bonds using a simple one- pot process (Scheme 1d).
Initially, the model reaction of 1-phenylbuta-2,3-dien-1-ol
(1a) and diisopropyl phosphonate ( 2a) was conducted to find
the optimal reaction conditions, including catalysts, ligands,
additives, solvents and temperatures. The results revealed that
the optimal conditions were as follows: 2 mol% Pd(acac)
2 as
the catalyst, 3 mol% xantphos as the ligand, 20 mol% H 3PO3
as the additive and tetrahydrofuran (THF) as the solvent at
80 1C under argon for 0.5 h with 1.1: 1 ratio of 1a/2a (see
Table S1 in the ESI † for details).
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand (Table S1,
entry 19, ESI †), the substrate scope of Pd-catalyzed coupling of
structurally diverse 1-substituted allenic alcohols with 2a was
first investigated. As shown in Table 1, the method was found
to be quite general and various 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes
could be conveniently and eﬃciently synthesized using this
facile and novel coupling. Generally, a wide range of 1-aryl buta-
2,3-dien-1-ols decorated with electron-donating groups and
electron-withdrawing groups on the phenyl ring, such as
halides ( 1b–1e), trifluoromethyl ( 1f), cyano ( 1g), methyl ( 1i),
methylthio ( 1j), ester ( 1k), methoxyl ( 1l), tert-butyl ( 1m) and
phenyl ( 1n), could be transformed into the corresponding
coupling products ( 3a–3n) in moderate to excellent yields,
without a distinct electronic effect on the reactivity being
observed. It is noteworthy that high selectivity for E stereo-
isomers of the above-mentioned products ( 3a–3r) was observed
owing to the steric hindrance on the basis of in situ
31P and
1H NMR spectroscopic analyses, 7,16 and the relative trace Z
stereoisomers were not isolated using column chromatography
on silica gel. To be noted, the catalytic efficiency was not altered
by changing the substituent R
1 to n-pentyl and phenylethynyl
(1s and 1t), but the corresponding products 3s and 3t were
obtained as a mixture of E/Z isomers in high total yields.
Interestingly, the simple buta-2,3-dien-1-ol 1u was also suitable
for the coupling, providing 3u in 72% yield.
To further verify the generality of this new coupling to
produce 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadienes, multisubstituted alle-
nic alcohols including 1,2-disubstituted, 1,4-disubstituted and
1,1,4-trisubstituted allenic alcohols were explored, and the
results are summarized in Table 2. Various tertiary 2,3-
allenols (1v–1aa) could be successfully engaged in this reaction,
affording the corresponding products 3v–3aa in high total
yields by enhancing the temperature and the loading of the
additive along with extending the reaction time. Fortunately,
the structural assignment was corroborated using X-ray crystal-
lography of product 3aa (CCDC† 2034498),
17 which clearly
disclosed that the phosphinoyl moiety was preferentially
installed at the C3-position of 1aa in this coupling. We next
investigated the effect of substitutions at the terminal position
of the allene moiety on the yield ( 1ab–1aj). When 1-aryl-4-alkyl
2,3-allenols ( 1ab–1ae) bearing F, CF
3 and CH 3 groups were
employed, excellent total yields of 89–94% with a high E/Z ratio
were obtained. Additionally, alkyl-substituted allenic alcohols
(1af and 1ag) could also participate in the coupling to afford the
target products 3af and 3ag, respectively, in high yields. Yet, the
allenic alcohols bearing a phenyl group at the C4 position ( 1ah
and 1ai) led to a marked decrease of the coupling yield ( 3ah,
41%; 3ai, 51%). To our delight, a 1,1,4-trisubstituted allenic
alcohol 1aj was proven to be viable for this coupling. Further-
more, it was noteworthy that the allenic alcohols with an aryl
moiety at the C1 position exhibited higher stereoselectivity for
E-isomers over those containing an alkyl group owing to the
effect of steric hindrance.
To further extend the scope of this reaction, some other
P(O)H substrates were then studied (Table 3). In addition to 2a,
other H-phosphonates such as dimethyl ( 2b), diethyl ( 2c),

dibutyl ( 2d) and diphenyl ( 2e) phosphonates could be used as
the suitable partners, generating the corresponding products
(3ak–3an) in moderate to excellent yields. To our satisfaction,
an H-phosphinate ester 2f proceeded smoothly to provide a
72% yield of product 3ao. However, the secondary phosphine
oxide 2g was inert under similar reaction conditions, which
might be attributed to the electronic properties of P(O)H
compounds.
To demonstrate the synthetic application of the present
method, a scaled-up reaction and further transformations of
some products were performed (Scheme 2). A gram-scale synth-
esis of 3u was conducted by using 20 mmol of 2a under similar
reaction conditions, producing 3u in 65% yield (Scheme 2a).
Moreover, 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadiene products could be
easily transformed to other useful compounds via Diels–Alder
reaction (Scheme 2b). As expected, 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-butadi-
enes like 3u could undergo Michael addition with common
nucleophiles such as 2i and 2g to generate the corresponding
products 5a and 5b in 77% and 51% yields, respectively
(Scheme 2c).
Based on the experimental facts and related literature
reports,
18 a plausible mechanism is presented in Scheme 3.
Initially, substrate 1a was activated through a hydrogen bond
interaction with phosphorous acid to generate the reactive
species A.18a Subsequently, palladium(0) attacked the C3-
position of A along with the cleavage of the C–O bond, leading
to the formation of allylpalladium hydroxide B, which was then
subjected to transmetalation with 2a (in the form of the
trivalent phosphine oxide 2a0) to result in intermediate C.18b–d
Finally, the reductive elimination of palladium species C
toward C–P bond formation occurred to give the coupling
product 3a and regenerated the palladium(0) catalyst.
18b,e
In conclusion, we have documented the first facile and
eﬃcient palladium-catalyzed direct cross-coupling reaction of
easily accessible allenic alcohols with various H-phosphonates,
furnishing a new and convenient route to synthesize a structu-
rally diverse array of novel multisubstituted 2-phosphinoyl-1,3-
butadienes along with the concurrent formation of new C–C,
CQC, and C–P bonds using a simple one-step process. The
obtained coupling products can be easily transformed into

useful multifunctionalized phosphonates via some simple reac-
tions. The salient features of this protocol are the excellent
chemo- and site selectivity, operational simplicity, remarkable
functional group tolerance, high atom- and step-economy and
good to excellent yields. Thus, we believe that this newly
developed approach would enrich the allene chemistry and
provide new scaffolds to construct valuable and complex mole-
cular skeletons.
